title: Queues and backpressure: where waiting goes
description: Run a batch with a slow job through a queue of 3 or 7 places and see whether the waiting builds up in the queue or at the producer.
initialCaption: Eight jobs wait in the producer. The queue in front of it has 3 places; job B is slow.
interactionHint: Drag to look around · scroll to zoom
fallback: While a slow job holds the single tool, waiting jobs fill the queue. With 3 places the producer cannot hand over the fourth job and is held; with 7 places the jobs wait in the queue instead. Either way the batch finishes at the same step, because the queue changes where work waits, not how fast the tool runs.
